🚨 BREAKING: Hackers are hitting supermarket freezers in 5 countries at the same time.

This is what Covid looked like in week 1. A few countries. Small numbers. Nobody called it a crisis.

1/ Sweden: stores say hackers hit their cooling overnight. One says fridges and freezers were set to 50°C, and the food spoiled. ICA Kvantum stores in Sjöbo and Tomelilla were hit, plus at least 6 Coop stores. Sjöbo stayed closed through the morning, threw out all affected goods and apologized. ICA says it is working to restore normal operations. In Sankt Olof a store manager said "everything is ruined." Sweden's National Cybersecurity Centre is working on several incidents.

2/ Estonia: the CEO of cooling firm Kitman Coldtech says several clients were targeted and a large chain's freezer was raised to +50°C. It was found and addressed in about 10 minutes, no major damage.

3/ Ireland: SuperValu pulled ALL fresh and frozen food from 13 stores. Its owner, Musgrave, confirmed a "cybersecurity incident" on a "specific model" of fridge.

4/ Luxembourg: Ahold Delhaize says an "IT incident" hit fridges and freezers at dozens of its supermarkets across Luxembourg and Belgium.

5/ Belgium: more than 40 Delhaize, at least 15 Carrefour and around 5 Spar stores were hit. Cold storage climbed to 15°C. Aisles were closed off and large amounts of stock were destroyed. A notice at one Proxy Delhaize said its systems had "fallen victim to hacking."

Now zoom out.

A freezer normally sits at -18°C. In Estonia, hackers reportedly got in through older controllers. In France, the controller maker said many devices were obsolete or ran outdated firmware. Raise the temperature overnight and the food rots. "You can't unspoil food," one professor said.

It did not start today. 3 weeks ago hackers raised freezers at more than 350 sites in France to as high as 50°C. There were fires. Intermarché's CEO put the cost at "tens of millions of euros nationwide in a single day." Sources suspect Russian involvement there. No group has claimed it. That same day an analyst said Spain, Portugal, Poland, Germany and Belgium were affected too.

Covid emptied the shelves. Nobody is calling this a crisis yet. But the Financial Times already puts the ruined food at millions of euros.

Officials say the Pentagon is treating late-August freezer failures on US military bases as a suspected hack. At least 6 base stores were hit. Army investigators are working with French law enforcement.

5 countries in one day. 11 countries named since August.

Share this. Everyone should know about it.

posts.text:
A nurse tries to trap Matt Walsh on abortion, demanding to know why he’d force a 13-year-old to give birth to her rapist’s child.

Then Walsh asks him one medical question, and the nurse wants to run away.

NURSE: “Why do you believe that a 13-year-old should be forced to give birth to their rapist’s child?”

WALSH: “I don’t think that it is ever okay to kill a child.”

Then he flips it.

WALSH: “You’re the medical expert. The unborn child, is that a human being or not?”

NURSE: “That is a religious question.”

WALSH: “It’s not a religious question. It’s a medical question. What is it if it’s not a human being?”

NURSE: “Medically speaking, we don’t consider it a full-fledged human being.”

WALSH: “What do you mean full-fledged?”

Instead of answering, the nurse pivots: why don’t we have “conception certificates”? Or “a heartbeat certificate”?

Walsh even agrees to the heartbeat certificate. But he keeps coming back to the one question.

“Is the unborn child a human being or not?”

Eventually, the nurse tries to bail.

NURSE: “I appreciate your time.”

WALSH: “No, no, no. Come back. Come back here.”

“You’re the medical expert, and you won’t even tell us what a human being is. I’m starting to get concerned.”

[crowd laughs]

Then Walsh sums it up:

“You have one side that can answer directly. It’s never okay to directly and intentionally kill a human child. That was my answer. I think I gave it probably 15, 20 times.

“And then you have the other side that has no answer at all to this question. What is a human child? Can’t even answer it.”

The nurse knew the answer. That’s why he left.

$MRVL TO ACQUIRE $LITE IN $115B ALL-STOCK DEAL

Marvell has agreed to acquire Lumentum in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $115B in enterprise value, combining two major suppliers of AI infrastructure and optical networking technology.

Under the agreement:

• Lumentum shareholders will receive 4.5 Marvell shares for each LITE share, implying roughly $1,132 per share.

• The offer represents a 23.9% premium to unaffected closing prices on October 28.

• Marvell shareholders will own approximately 67% of the combined company, with Lumentum shareholders holding 33%.

The deal brings together Marvell's custom AI chips, networking switches and interconnect technology with Lumentum's lasers, optical transceivers and optical circuit switching capabilities.

The bigger opportunity is the growing shift from copper to optical connectivity as AI data centers require faster data transfer, greater bandwidth and improved power efficiency.

Marvell says the combination could expand its addressable market to $550B, allowing it to offer more integrated connectivity solutions across AI data centers and within advanced chip packages.

The companies also expect:

• More than $1B in annual run-rate cost synergies.

• Improved long-term revenue growth and profit margins.

• Accretion to Marvell's adjusted EPS in the first year after closing.

Matt Murphy will remain CEO of the combined company, with the transaction expected to close in H1 2028, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.

Separately, Marvell reaffirmed the midpoint of its fiscal Q3 revenue guidance while narrowing the expected range to ±2% from ±5%.

Following the Lumentum / Marvell deal: 

My opinion is that independent Western laser players, like $AAOI, $COHR, and $SIVE became a lot more strategically valuable. 

$MTSI and $SMTC should get some attention too as emerging laser players in 2027. 

If I had to guess: 

1. Companies competing against Marvell, or not in the $NVDA ecosystem bandwagon, such as $AMD, are likely going to rethink their relationship with $LITE.

If getting bottlenecked by Nvidia capacity agreements wasn't enough... Incentives around qualifying + bringing up other laser players, seems very necessary now. 

Since you generally don't want competitors like Marvell to have influence or visibility over your roadmaps, IP, capacity, pricing, etc. even if there is a "firewall".  

2. $MRVL acquiring Lumentum opened pandoras box in a way of acquiring a critical chokepoint all your competitors + buyers use. 

$LITE was used by your major hyperscalers and across AI supply chains. 

Now, your leaders might wonder if weaponizing capacity agreements might not be as effective.... If someone else can just buy the entire company. 

There's only a few major public merchant Western players out there, and I'm also sure many others will want to follow the Marvell / Broadcom route via vertical integration, given I think $MRVL saves around $1B+ in costs/year. 

So M&A premiums likely went up. 

$SMTC was actively looking to buy laser capacity via M&A so I'm sure they're looking at $SIVE given their 100M CW DFB laser expansion + tiny MC. 

$JBL also probably wants to vertically integrate down the road too so $SIVE is also an acquisition target for their 1.6T program. 

$AMD was looking for ELSFP + CW capacity given Nvidia bottlenecks, so I'm sure they've looked at $AAOI. 

can go on and on about other ASIC players (like in Taiwan) that likely are looking at vertical integration too.

Since multiple players use a small subset of laser suppliers, if competitors just go ahead and buys them... 

There's a lot pressure to M&A for their own supply chain defensibility. 

TLDR: Independent laser suppliers should capture a material strategic revaluation since $MRVL + $LITE, sets a new precedent + implications. 

We'll see what happens.
